newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Kashmir leader says 14 killed by car bomb.
newsitem.headline: Indian Kashmir leader says 14 killed by car bomb.

text.p: At least 14 people died on Saturday and more than 50 were injured, some seriously, when a powerful car bomb exploded in the northern city of Jammu, the leader of India's Jammu and Kashmir state said.

"There was only one blast, not two as previously reported," Farooq Abdullah told Reuters by telephone from Jammu, the state's winter capital. "We strongly condemn this attack. Innocent people have died. Terrorism must stop."
Earlier reports had said there were two blasts in the city's crowded central bus station.

Abdullah said the bomb was planted in a Gypsy, an all-terrain vehicle. "There were a lot of vehicles moving around. We don't know if the Gypsy was moving at the time. It destroyed a bus next to it. I have just come back from the hospital and a number of people have been injured by flying metal and glass. One man was very seriously injured."

The blast occurred on the second day of crucial talks between Indian and Pakistani diplomats in New Delhi. The bitter rivals have fought two wars since independence from Britain in 1947 over the Himalayan territory of Kashmir.

Asked if authorities had any clues as to who had planted the bomb, Abdullah said: "There are a number of people who do not want the talks to succeed. We are trying to determine the origin of the car bomb."
